promise.title: Deleted after processing — exceptions listed below
promise.sub: Every line below is checkable in our source — we only claim what is true today.
promise.item1Title: Single-step tools: gone when the response ends
promise.item1Body: The upload and the result are deleted in the same response. Nothing is archived or indexed. Tools that take several steps are the exception — each is listed below.
promise.item2Title: Uncollected files last at most 7 days
promise.item2Body: A daily sweeper clears entries in the temporary directory older than 7 days, for every user alike. Redaction session directories are the exception — see below.
promise.item3Title: No file names or contents in the usage ledger
promise.item3Body: It holds the module name, duration, outcome and a request id — enough to count which tool ran, not enough to reconstruct a single file.
promise.note1Body: MD to DOCX, Format DOCX and Print Split all run as generate-then-download, so both your upload and the result stay in a server temporary directory until you take them, and are cleared after at most 7 days.
promise.note2Title: Exception: PDF Redaction and PDF Editor
promise.note2Body: A redaction upload stays on the server while you mark it up: it is deleted when you download, and the page tries to notify the server when you leave. An abandoned session is only reclaimed the next time someone opens that tool, by an expiry sweep. Page images rendered when you open a file in PDF Editor stay in the temporary directory for at most 7 days; the upload itself is deleted immediately.
promise.note3Title: We do log IP and browser
promise.note3Body: Those two columns are the only basis for unique-visitor counts. The IP comes from the X-Forwarded-For proxy header (or the direct connection address when there is no proxy), and the user agent is truncated to 200 characters.
promise.note4Title: Operational logs may carry file paths
promise.note4Body: When a deletion fails or an exception is thrown, the operational log records the temporary file path and a stack trace; the path may contain the name you uploaded with. Those logs are kept for 30 days. The usage ledger holds none of this.
